axes.ability_corr_worst.note: largest |correlation| between a user's position on a shipped axis and their fitted ability; positions re-derived as the penalized MLE against the shipped loadings, abilities and response parameters, which the fit does not persist

axes.rating_leak_worst.note: largest correlation between one END of a shipped axis (the shared tail weight of +g or -g) and one of the shipped per-problem quantities (rating, slope, floor), over every fitted problem — the quantity the rating-orthogonality penalty is scored on

axes.taught_agreement_mean.note: hinged tail agreement (z >= 1.0) between each axis's taught end and the rule column it was taught from, meaned over the 7 axes, on attempted+banked problems

axes.taught_agreement_min.note: the same agreement at the weakest-held axis

axistail.axes_measured.note: axes with an untaught tail, i.e. taught by a single rule; the 0 two-sided axes have no untaught end and are excluded

axistail.taught_never_max.note: largest never-attempted share among the axes' taught, named tails (1000 most extreme problems each)

axistail.taught_never_min.note: smallest never-attempted share among the axes' taught, named tails (1000 most extreme problems each)

axistail.untaught_exceeds_taught_axes.note: axes whose UNTAUGHT tail holds the larger never-attempted share of the two, over each tail's 1000 most extreme problems

axistail.untaught_never_max.note: largest never-attempted share among the axes' untaught tails (1000 most extreme problems each)

axistail.untaught_never_min.note: smallest never-attempted share among the axes' untaught tails (1000 most extreme problems each)

barrier.off_rating_high.note: …and the 99.9th percentile, the high side; averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

barrier.off_rating_high_seed_ratio.note: how many times the barrier-off arm's 99.9th rating percentile moved between the panel's seeds — the blow-out HAPPENS every time, while its size is not itself a reproducible quantity, which is what an unbounded tail does

barrier.off_rating_low.note: 0.1th percentile of the derived rating with the slope barrier removed — the low side of the blow-out. A per-fit property, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

barrier.off_slope_at_floor_pct.note: share of slopes on the clamp with the barrier removed, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

barrier.off_stop_cost_mnat.note: the same paired held-out cost read at the FINAL epoch — the fit that would actually ship, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

barrier.off_stop_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when every seed puts the barrier-off cost on the same side of zero on BOTH readings, 0 when the seeds disagree. An indicator for a `fig-guard: barrier.off_stop_cost_sign_consistent == 1` beside any sentence naming the direction of that cost, never for a span

barrier.off_stop_tail_cost_mnat.note: held-out (stop-split) cost of removing the barrier over the last third of the budget, millinats — PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed, then meaned over the seeds. The headline reading: it is the level the arm settled at, which a final checkpoint alone samples only once

barrier.shipped_no_rating_max.note: and the most, in a run differing only in the seed. The pair is the figure: this count is a property of a particular fit and not of the model, so it is re-read after a refit rather than carried

barrier.shipped_no_rating_min.note: fewest problems left with no defined rating — a floor at or above the calibration probability — across the panel's runs of the SHIPPED configuration

barrier.shipped_rating_span.note: p0.1..p99.9 span of the derived rating as SHIPPED, the same per-fit property the two arms above are compared against, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds — without it neither blow-out nor compression has a reference

barrier.shipped_wander_range_mnat.note: the same wander as a peak-to-peak range, averaged over the seeds — how far apart two honest single-arm readings of one configuration can land

barrier.shipped_wander_sd_mnat.note: standard deviation of the SHIPPED arm's own held-out score across the last third of its budget, millinats, averaged over the seeds — the panel's resolution floor. No contrast smaller than this is resolved by one arm per configuration, which is why every configuration here is replicated

barrier.tenx_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when every seed puts the ten-times cost on the same side of zero on both readings. An indicator for a fig-guard, not a span

barrier.tenx_no_rating_mean.note: the same count at ten times the barrier weight, seed-averaged — the one cost of a heavier barrier the held-out likelihood cannot show, since the problems it touches ship a sentinel rather than a wrong number

barrier.tenx_rating_span.note: p0.1..p99.9 span of the derived rating at ten times the barrier weight — the compression the weight is swept against. A per-fit property, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

barrier.tenx_stop_cost_mnat.note: the same cost read at the FINAL epoch, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

barrier.tenx_stop_tail_cost_mnat.note: held-out cost of TEN TIMES the barrier weight over the last third of the budget, millinats, paired within a seed and then meaned, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. §1.7 chooses the weight by held-out sweep and names ten times as the failure direction, so where that arm lands is part of the claim: negative means the heavier barrier fits BETTER than what ships

cast.contrast_finer_one_in.note: one in how many of those within-problem comparisons is finer than the worst-case cast error

cast.contrast_median_sd.note: median |answer cell - alternative cell| per axis, over the variation cells of a seeded sample of published problems — the within-problem distinction the tendency sign test draws

cast.p999_sd.note: the same bound at the 99.9th percentile of published per-cell values

cast.worst_sd.note: largest half-precision rounding error the published per-cell motif vectors can carry, in axis standard deviations (the loadings are gauged to unit RMS, so a raw unit is one)

community.gate_shift_ranks.note: ranks the mean shown rank moves when every player active in the 7-day window is counted instead of those carrying a rank (30+ valid buffered attempts)

community.gate_shift_signed.note: the same shift with its sign — negative when dropping the gate moves the mean toward the weaker end

corpus.expected_id_collisions.note: expected accidental id collisions among the published problems, n(n-1)/2^33 — each one a silently discarded candidate, never a corrupted record

corpus.id_rejection_odds.note: one-in-N odds that a fresh candidate's id is already taken, 2^32/n

corpus.never_attempted_pct.note: share of the published problems with no first-time human attempt in the attempt log

corpus.pass_not_last_13_pct.note: share of published 13×13 problems whose pass variation is not the last one, so the placeholder row it gets in the per-cell block is what keeps every later row on its own variation

corpus.pass_not_last_9_pct.note: share of published 9×9 problems whose pass variation is not the last one, so the placeholder row it gets in the per-cell block is what keeps every later row on its own variation

corpus.problems_13.note: published 13×13 problems, to the nearest thousand

corpus.problems_9.note: published 9×9 problems, to the nearest thousand

corpus.problems_total.note: problems in the published index, to the nearest thousand

curve.dan_vs_cheapest_max.note: widest dan-range segment ÷ the curve's cheapest segment

curve.dan_vs_cheapest_min.note: cheapest dan-range segment ÷ the curve's cheapest segment

curve.first_second_gradient_ratio.note: the curve's SECOND segment ÷ its FIRST in rank per rating unit — how far a rank-space slope jumps across that one knot

curve.knot_rank_strong.note: strongest knot of the published rating→rank curve, in internal rank (the strong edge of the strongest band it covers)

curve.knot_rank_weak.note: weakest knot of the published rating→rank curve, in internal rank (integers are band edges, so this is the weak edge of that band)

curve.knot_rating_span.note: rating distance between the curve's outermost knots

curve.rating_per_rank_cheapest.note: rating units one rank costs on the curve's CHEAPEST segment

curve.rating_per_rank_cheapest_at.note: band the cheapest segment spans (its weak-edge knot)

curve.rating_per_rank_dan_max.note: widest segment through the dan range — segments starting in [+0, +9) in internal rank, the 1d…9d bands

curve.rating_per_rank_dan_min.note: cheapest segment through the dan range — segments starting in [+0, +9) in internal rank, the 1d…9d bands

curve.rating_per_rank_weak_edge.note: rating units one rank costs on the outermost weak-side segment

determinism.repeat_files_compared.note: output files compared across all repeats — the size of the check behind the zero above

determinism.repeat_files_differing.note: the same over EVERY output a run writes, the model checkpoint and the axis artifacts included

determinism.repeat_pairs.note: independent repeats found among the refit panels' arms — pairs of separate processes that ran one configuration on one machine at one revision

determinism.repeat_problem_files_differi.note: per-problem output files that differ between the two runs of a repeat. §1.8's bitwise claim is this being zero, which is what a fig-guard holds it to, not a number worth quoting

determinism.repeat_problems.note: problems whose full parameter row was compared in each repeat

determinism.repeat_traces_identical.note: 1 when every repeat's held-out convergence trace matches value for value, 0 otherwise — the training path itself repeating, not only what it wrote

draw.info_argmax_enrichment.note: on the worst named motif tail (ko), how much more often the top-information candidate of a pool of 50 sits in that tail than the pool itself does, over rank-prior-weighted pools on both board sizes

draw.info_best_over_pool.note: the best candidate's Fisher information over the pool's mean, averaged over the same pools

draw.info_fifth_advantage.note: the fifth-best candidate's share of the best candidate's advantage over the pool mean, over the same pools

draw.info_slice_over_best.note: the information a uniform draw from the top 20% of the pool carries against the top candidate's own — what the slot gives up by not argmaxing

features.pca128_holdout_bce.note: held-out-PROBLEM cross-entropy at a joint-PCA activation width of 128, nats per attempt, meaned over the last third of the budget and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. A level, not a comparison: the seeds hold aside different problems

features.pca128_slope_median.note: median fitted per-problem slope at a width of 128, over every fitted problem, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

features.pca128_wins_both_sides.note: 1 when the shipped width scores better held out than BOTH its neighbours in the swept set (64 below, 256 above) at every seed, on the last-third reading — §1.3's 'wins from both sides' as one indicator

features.pca16_cost_mnat.note: held-out-problem cost of a width of 16 against the shipped 128, millinats over the last third of the budget, signed (positive = worse than the shipped width). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

features.pca16_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when both seeds put the 16-against-128 contrast on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

features.pca16_holdout_bce.note: held-out-PROBLEM cross-entropy at a joint-PCA activation width of 16, nats per attempt, meaned over the last third of the budget and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. A level, not a comparison: the seeds hold aside different problems

features.pca16_slope_median.note: median fitted per-problem slope at a width of 16, over every fitted problem, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

features.pca256_cost_mnat.note: held-out-problem cost of a width of 256 against the shipped 128, millinats over the last third of the budget, signed (positive = worse than the shipped width). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

features.pca256_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when both seeds put the 256-against-128 contrast on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

features.pca256_highest_slope.note: 1 when the 256-wide arm carries the highest median slope of any arm at every seed — the memorization signature §1.3 names, as an indicator

features.pca256_holdout_bce.note: held-out-PROBLEM cross-entropy at a joint-PCA activation width of 256, nats per attempt, meaned over the last third of the budget and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. A level, not a comparison: the seeds hold aside different problems

features.pca256_slope_median.note: median fitted per-problem slope at a width of 256, over every fitted problem, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

features.pca64_cost_mnat.note: held-out-problem cost of a width of 64 against the shipped 128, millinats over the last third of the budget, signed (positive = worse than the shipped width). PAIRED inside a seed — both arms hold aside the same problems — and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

features.pca64_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when both seeds put the 64-against-128 contrast on the same side of zero on the last-third reading, 0 when they disagree — the two seeds being independent estimates of one paired delta. An indicator for a fig-guard beside a sentence naming that contrast's direction, not for a span

features.pca64_holdout_bce.note: held-out-PROBLEM cross-entropy at a joint-PCA activation width of 64, nats per attempt, meaned over the last third of the budget and then averaged over the panel's 2 seeds. A level, not a comparison: the seeds hold aside different problems

features.pca64_slope_median.note: median fitted per-problem slope at a width of 64, over every fitted problem, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

history.rank_gap_career_excess.note: how much WIDER the career arm's spread reads than the per-block arm's, in percentage points of the more-than-2-ranks share — what within-career drift adds once it is no longer taken out. Positive means the career arm is wider

history.rank_gap_median.note: median gap in ranks; the player's rating is fitted over their own consecutive 500-attempt block, so within-career drift is out; over first-time attempts whose problem still ships and whose 500-attempt block has an anchor rating; the gap in ranks is the player's rank minus the problem's, each mapped through the SHIPPED rating→rank curve and then differenced

history.rank_gap_median_career.note: median gap in ranks; the player's rating is one anchor over their whole first-time history, scored on exactly the rows the block arm scores so the two are paired; over first-time attempts whose problem still ships and whose 500-attempt block has an anchor rating; the gap in ranks is the player's rank minus the problem's, each mapped through the SHIPPED rating→rank curve and then differenced

history.rank_gap_over2_career_pct.note: share of attempts more than 2 ranks from the player's rank; the player's rating is one anchor over their whole first-time history, scored on exactly the rows the block arm scores so the two are paired; over first-time attempts whose problem still ships and whose 500-attempt block has an anchor rating; the gap in ranks is the player's rank minus the problem's, each mapped through the SHIPPED rating→rank curve and then differenced

history.rank_gap_over2_pct.note: share of attempts more than 2 ranks from the player's rank; the player's rating is fitted over their own consecutive 500-attempt block, so within-career drift is out; over first-time attempts whose problem still ships and whose 500-attempt block has an anchor rating; the gap in ranks is the player's rank minus the problem's, each mapped through the SHIPPED rating→rank curve and then differenced

history.rank_gap_over3_career_pct.note: share of attempts more than 3 ranks from the player's rank; the player's rating is one anchor over their whole first-time history, scored on exactly the rows the block arm scores so the two are paired; over first-time attempts whose problem still ships and whose 500-attempt block has an anchor rating; the gap in ranks is the player's rank minus the problem's, each mapped through the SHIPPED rating→rank curve and then differenced

history.rank_gap_over3_pct.note: share of attempts more than 3 ranks from the player's rank; the player's rating is fitted over their own consecutive 500-attempt block, so within-career drift is out; over first-time attempts whose problem still ships and whose 500-attempt block has an anchor rating; the gap in ranks is the player's rank minus the problem's, each mapped through the SHIPPED rating→rank curve and then differenced

lr.net_slow_converge_epoch.note: the same epoch for the three-times-slower network, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

lr.net_slow_converge_ratio.note: how many times longer the slower network takes to reach its own plateau, at the same held-out margin — the second averaged epoch over the first, so above 1 means the slower network plateaus later

lr.net_slow_cost_mnat.note: the same cost of a three-times-slower network at the shipped field rate; signed, positive means the slower network is the worse fit. The claim is a tie, read at the last checkpoint both traces are finite — the final epoch for an arm that stayed finite, and the fit that would actually ship; PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed — one seed is one held-out draw, so the arms inside it hold aside the same stop rows — then meaned over the 2 seeds

lr.net_slow_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when every seed puts this cost on the same side of zero on BOTH readings, 0 when the seeds disagree. An indicator for a `fig-guard: lr.net_slow_cost_sign_consistent == 1` beside any sentence naming the direction of that cost, never for a span

lr.net_slow_tail_cost_mnat.note: held-out (stop-split) cost of a three-times-slower network at the shipped field rate; signed, positive means the slower network is the worse fit. The claim is a tie, millinats, over the last third of the budget — PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed — one seed is one held-out draw, so the arms inside it hold aside the same stop rows — then meaned over the 2 seeds. The headline reading: it is the level the arm settled at, which a final checkpoint alone samples only once

lr.ratio10x_cost_mnat.note: the same cost at a ten-fold field/net ratio against the shipped ~33-fold — the bottom of the saturating region, read at the last checkpoint both traces are finite — the final epoch for an arm that stayed finite, and the fit that would actually ship; PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed — one seed is one held-out draw, so the arms inside it hold aside the same stop rows — then meaned over the 2 seeds

lr.ratio10x_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when every seed puts this cost on the same side of zero on BOTH readings, 0 when the seeds disagree. An indicator for a `fig-guard: lr.ratio10x_cost_sign_consistent == 1` beside any sentence naming the direction of that cost, never for a span

lr.ratio10x_tail_cost_mnat.note: held-out (stop-split) cost at a ten-fold field/net ratio against the shipped ~33-fold — the bottom of the saturating region, millinats, over the last third of the budget — PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed — one seed is one held-out draw, so the arms inside it hold aside the same stop rows — then meaned over the 2 seeds. The headline reading: it is the level the arm settled at, which a final checkpoint alone samples only once

lr.shared_rate_cost_mnat.note: the same cost of one shared rate against the shipped split, read at the last checkpoint both traces are finite — the final epoch for an arm that stayed finite, and the fit that would actually ship; PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed — one seed is one held-out draw, so the arms inside it hold aside the same stop rows — then meaned over the 2 seeds

lr.shared_rate_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when every seed puts this cost on the same side of zero on BOTH readings, 0 when the seeds disagree. An indicator for a `fig-guard: lr.shared_rate_cost_sign_consistent == 1` beside any sentence naming the direction of that cost, never for a span

lr.shared_rate_diverge_epoch.note: the earliest epoch at which any seed's single-shared-rate arm first met that test; 0 means no seed did

lr.shared_rate_diverged.note: 1 when the single-shared-rate arm (field rate pulled onto the network's) diverged at ANY seed, 0 when it did so at none — non-finite, or 20 millinats above its own running best held-out score. The claim is that one shared rate CAN blow up, so one seed doing it is the finding. An indicator for a fig-guard, not a span

lr.shared_rate_tail_cost_mnat.note: held-out (stop-split) cost of one shared rate against the shipped split, millinats, over the last third of the budget — PAIRED against the shipped arm of its own seed — one seed is one held-out draw, so the arms inside it hold aside the same stop rows — then meaned over the 2 seeds. The headline reading: it is the level the arm settled at, which a final checkpoint alone samples only once

lr.shipped_converge_epoch.note: first epoch from which the shipped arm's held-out score never again rises above its own final value by more than its own closing spread — the band it settles into, each arm measured against the band it actually reaches. A per-fit property, averaged over the panel's 2 seeds

motif.altstat_crossproj_manifest_pct.note: the same rate against the shard manifest's copy of that vector

motif.altstat_crossproj_setwide_pct.note: share of a 20000-problem seeded sample whose published availability masses move when the reference is taken from the set-wide correct-move sidecar instead of the problem's own per-cell block

motif.depth_null_axes_better.note: axes where the shipped visits-weighted null beats the equal-count one on per-error directional log-loss with the paired 95% bootstrap interval clear of zero, of 7 measured

motif.depth_null_pooled_gain.note: nats of directional log-loss per scored error the visits-weighted null saves over the equal-count one, pooled over axes

motif.fitted_null_gain_share_pct.note: what the fitted null adds over the shipped visits-weighted one, pooled, as a share of that null's own gain over equal counting

motif.fixed_null_most_reliable_axes.note: axes on which the RETIRED fixed-even null is the most split-half reliable of the 6 parameter-free arms — a constant says the same thing about every problem, so reliability rewards it for carrying no information. The claim is that it wins everywhere, which is what a fig-guard holds this to

motif.fixed_null_reliability_gain.note: how far ahead it sits: mean over axes of its split-half rank correlation minus the uniform null's, on the same users and the same paired resamples

motif.fixed_null_worst_flag_pct.note: share of testable users the retired fixed-50% test flags on that axis

motif.menu_worst_toward_pct.note: toward-side share of offered-alternative weight on the most menu-skewed axis (yose)

motif.null_axes_measured.note: shipped axes the availability-null measurement runs over

motif.null_sign_reversals.note: axes whose population error lean changes sign between the fixed even split and the shipped visits-linear availability null

motif.shipped_null_worst_flag_pct.note: share of testable users the shipped null's test flags on that axis

motif.tendency_rank_share_population_pct.note: largest per-axis share of the between-user variance the user's rank alone explains when the lean is scored against a population average instead of each problem's own null (ko)

motif.tendency_rank_share_shipped_pct.note: the same share for the reading that ships, scored against each problem's own availability null (yose)

motif.tendency_rank_users.note: accounts with a fitted ability and at least 10 scored errors on the axis the share below is measured on

penalty.free_slope_corr.note: largest |whole-axis correlation| with SLOPE in the free control (no rating-orthogonality penalty, no teaching pull) — an unheld axis spent on a shipped response parameter, and on the slope rather than on difficulty

penalty.free_stop_cost_mnat.note: the free control's held-out (stop-split) cost against the shipped arm, millinats, paired rows at one seed

penalty.per_tail_leak.note: worst per-tail |cosine| under the SHIPPED penalty, which scores the two ends separately — what penalizing per tail cuts the worst end to, measured on the panel's own shipped arm

penalty.unpenalized_tail_leak.note: worst per-tail |cosine| with the rating-orthogonality penalty removed — what the axes absorb when nothing holds them off the shipped quantities

penalty.whole_axis_reported.note: worst whole-axis |correlation| between an axis and one of the shipped per-problem quantities (rating, slope, floor) in the arm penalized on the whole axis — the statistic that arm optimises, over every fitted problem

penalty.whole_axis_tail_leak.note: the same arm's worst PER-TAIL |cosine|: one hinged axis END against one centred shipped quantity, the ends being the only part of an axis a name is read off

penalty.whole_axis_understatement.note: how many fold the whole-axis statistic understates what the ends of the same fit carry — the second figure over the first

published.floor_above_calibration.note: published problems whose floor exceeds the calibration probability 0.8, so their rating is a sentinel rather than an 80%-clear point

published.floor_above_calibration_rank_s.note: strongest rank a sentinel rating maps to

published.floor_above_calibration_rank_w.note: weakest rank a sentinel rating maps to through the published curve

published.floor_between_clamp_and_calibr.note: published problems with a floor in (0.78, 0.8] — clamped by the client despite a defined rating; the clamp catches only the sentinel problems exactly while this is zero

published.floor_max.note: largest guessing floor among the published problems

published.floor_near_calibration.note: published problems with a floor in [0.75, 0.8] — the approach band, below the threshold

published.floor_p999.note: guessing floor at the 99.9th percentile of the published set

rank.declaration_noise_lo.note: declaration noise the federation spread implies once the verified spread is subtracted in quadrature

rank.declaration_noise_ratio_lo.note: that noise against the spread the publicly-checkable users show

rank.declarations_screened.note: declarations the mapping screened out as junk before its final fit, and which nothing here scores

rank.declaring_median_rank.note: …of everyone who declared a rank anywhere

rank.deep_kyu_mae.note: mean absolute residual against declarations at 15 kyu and weaker, in ranks

rank.exact_match_beyond1.note: of them sitting more than a rank from their verified rating

rank.exact_match_displacement.note: their mean self-report minus verified rating, in ranks

rank.exact_match_in_band.note: of them declaring exactly the band their verified rating falls in

rank.exact_match_miss_narrowest.note: narrowest miss among the out-of-band ones, as a distance to the declared band's edge

rank.exact_match_users.note: users holding both a self-report and a verified rating on that same ladder

rank.exact_match_widest_share.note: share of the exact-match mean the two widest-missing rows carry between them

rank.games_equivalent.note: tournament games per player at which two independent ratings agree as well as the shown rank agrees with a declared EGF rank

rank.games_equivalent_sd.note: its bootstrap SD over the declarations behind the target

rank.games_n.note: EGF declarations the match rests on

rank.honesty_ci_hi.note: highest 95% upper bound it reaches — what the data licenses as an upper limit on inflation

rank.honesty_lo.note: displacement of a self-report from a verified rating at the same fitted rank, lowest reading over both routes; + = self-reports claim stronger

rank.honesty_matched_lo.note: the rank-matched route alone, lowest over the matching tolerances

rank.honesty_se.note: widest standard error the rank-matched route carries

rank.honesty_selfreporters.note: users they are matched against: self-reporters holding no verified rating

rank.honesty_verified.note: users with a machine-written federation rating, the contrast's binding count

rank.linkable_median_rank.note: median fitted rank of the users holding a verified rating

rank.rho.note: per-server Spearman(mapped rating, declared rank), n-weighted, self-declarations

rank.rho_se.note: bootstrap SE of rank.rho over players

rank.route_gap.note: exact-match reading minus the rank-matched one at the one-rank tolerance: what being publicly checkable is worth

rank.server_mean_max_t.note: largest per-server residual mean in units of its own standard error — nominal significance is 1.96, before any correction for looking at all of them

rank.servers_scored.note: servers carrying enough declarations for a residual mean and its error

rank.spread_survey_egf.note: …against self-reports on the federation coupling, same range

rank.spread_survey_pooled.note: …against self-reports pooled over every server, same range

rank.spread_verified.note: spread of the residual against verified ratings, over their own fitted-rank range

rank.stone_value_kyu_logit.note: logits one band buys, averaged over 15k–5k, from the even-game table's joint stone-value fit

rank.within1_pct.note: self-declarations with the shown server rank within one rank of the declared

rank.within_se_pts.note: larger bootstrap SE of the two within-shares, percentage points

rankmap.consensus_dan_bias.note: …the same error over the same rows under the shipped mapping, where the federation is one coupling among many

rankmap.federation_dan_bias.note: mean signed error against dan-band declarations, in the declaring server's own units, with the federation the identity hub the latent is defined by (negative = placed weaker than they declare)

rankmap.federation_dan_shift.note: how far a latent anchored on the federation alone moves the shown rank of the surveyed users the shipped mapping places in the dan bands, in ranks (positive = shown stronger)

rankmap.federation_kyu_shift.note: …and of those it places in the kyu bands

rankmap.screen_curve_shift.note: largest displacement between the screened and unscreened rating→rank curves at equal rank, over the ladder they span, in rating units

rankmap.screen_likelihood_bar.note: loosest one-in-N ordinal likelihood a declared category must fall below for the mixture's junk posterior to pass one half, over the servers' fitted couplings

rankmap.screen_mildest_miss.note: smallest miss among the declarations the screen removes: how far the mapping places that user from the band they declared, in ranks

rankmap.screen_rank_shift.note: the same displacement at equal RATING, in ranks — the largest gap between the two curves anywhere on the ladder

recall.clean_chain_excluded_pct.note: share of repeat attempts excluded by the clean-chain filter (chains beginning before repeats were reliably logged)

recall.cochran_q.note: Cochran's heterogeneity statistic for the per-user step at the 5-events-per-cell cut

recall.constant_deficit_nats.note: held-out nats the retention computation trails a constant rate by

recall.direction_share_min20_pct.note: share of those users whose own odds ratio runs in the expected direction, at the 20-events cut

recall.direction_share_min5_pct.note: share of those users whose own odds ratio runs in the expected direction, at the 5-events cut

recall.free_rung_gain_nats.note: held-out nats a free effect per rung buys — the upper bound on any reshaping of the streak term

recall.matched_ratio_era_gap.note: absolute pre/post gap of the matched contrast — the check that stratifying removed the schedule change

recall.matched_ratio_or.note: within-(user, matched relative-interval band) MH odds of clearing, post-success vs post-lapse — schedule-invariant, all eras pooled

recall.matched_ratio_or_pre.note: the same contrast on serves before the first-success step entered the schedule

recall.matched_step_interval.note: interval multiplier the matched contrast implies at the post-lapse operating rate

recall.mh_plateau_or_sd.note: separation of the second success from the first, in sd, within user

recall.mh_step_or_sd.note: separation of the post-success from the post-lapse state, in sd, within user

recall.no_post_success_users_pct.note: users with no post-success rows inside the window the on-device model trains on

recall.pooled_or_min10.note: pooled within-user post-lapse/post-success odds ratio, users with at least 10 events in each cell

recall.pooled_or_min20.note: pooled within-user post-lapse/post-success odds ratio, users with at least 20 events in each cell

recall.pooled_or_min5.note: pooled within-user post-lapse/post-success odds ratio, users with at least 5 events in each cell

recall.post_success_rows_median.note: median post-success rows per user inside that same window

recall.recalibration_overspread.note: reciprocal of that slope: how many times too wide the model's spread is

recall.recalibration_slope.note: held-out Platt slope on the retention model's own log-odds, split by user

recall.rung0_clear_high.note: highest post-lapse clear rate across those same bins

recall.rung0_clear_low.note: lowest post-lapse clear rate across elapsed-gap bins from 0.5 to 16 days

recall.rung0_clear_poststep.note: post-lapse clear rate over the same serves — the parity target

recall.rung0_clear_rate.note: pooled post-lapse clear rate, against the 0.80 window-open ceiling

recall.rung0_composition_points.note: post-lapse clear-rate points, users who reach the next rung minus users who never do; negative means composition suppresses the step

recall.rung0_gap_trend_points.note: post-lapse clear-rate points per doubling of the elapsed gap over those bins; positive is a rise, not decay

recall.rung1_clear_poststep.note: realized clear of first-rung serves since the step settled

recall.rung_step_logodds_rise.note: rise in mean cold-solve log-odds from the post-lapse to the post-success state

recall.rung_step_model_visible_share.note: that multiplier as a share of the interval correction the realized rates require at the first success

recall.rung_step_model_visible_stability.note: stability multiplier the difficulty term already draws from that rise

recall.rung_up_clear_prestep.note: realized clear of rung >= 1 serves scheduled without the step — the diagnosis-era anchor

recall.step_form_gain_nats.note: held-out nats a first-success step buys over the shipped linear streak term

seeds.axes_matched.note: axes matched per pair — K as shipped

seeds.problems_scored.note: problems every agreement above is measured over: attempted at least once (first-time attempts) and carried by every arm

seeds.taught_cross_seed_mean.note: the same statistic for two fits of the SHIPPED configuration differing only in the seed — the teaching pull on

seeds.teaching_cost_final_mnat.note: the same cost read at the final epoch alone — the epoch that would actually ship

seeds.teaching_cost_mnat.note: what the constant pull costs on held-out rows, millinats, positive meaning the taught fit predicts worse. Paired: the taught and untaught arms at one seed hold aside the same rows. Each arm is read as the mean over the last third of its budget, the two same-seed pairs then averaged

seeds.teaching_cost_sign_consistent.note: 1 when both same-seed pairs put the cost on the same side of zero under both readings, 0 otherwise. An indicator for a fig-guard: it is what says the sign is a finding rather than the wander of a single pair

seeds.teaching_gap.note: taught minus untaught cross-seed agreement, on the means — what the constant pull toward the rule columns buys in basis stability, the two measured on the same problems

seeds.untaught_cross_seed_mean.note: cross-seed direction agreement with the teaching pull off: axes matched one-to-one between two fits by maximum total |correlation| of their per-problem loadings, each matched pair's |correlation| meaned over the 7 axes and then over the three untaught seed pairs, on attempted problems

seeds.untaught_cross_seed_min.note: the same agreement at each untaught pair's weakest-matched axis, averaged over the three pairs

sefloor.dan_min.note: tightest SE floor over the dan range, in ranks — knots in [+0, +9) in internal rank, the 1d…9d bands

sefloor.kyu_vs_dan_ratio.note: mean floor over the middle kyus ÷ mean floor over the dan range, each an unweighted mean over that region's knots ([-15, -5) in internal rank, the 15k…6k bands; [+0, +9) in internal rank, the 1d…9d bands) — the TYPICAL kyu-vs-dan comparison, not the extremes

sefloor.midkyu_max.note: loosest SE floor over the middle kyus, in ranks — knots in [-15, -5) in internal rank, the 15k…6k bands

sefloor.spread_ratio.note: loosest middle-kyu floor ÷ tightest dan-range floor — the spread between the extremes a constant floor would have to cover

sefloor.weak_trough.note: tightest SE floor within 2 ranks of the rating→rank curve's weakest knot, in ranks — the weak-end trough, which is a different feature from the ridge at the 1k/1d boundary

serve.clear_100_300.note: clear rate over positions 101-300; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.clear_25_100.note: clear rate over positions 26-100; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.clear_after300.note: clear rate past position 300; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history. Also the rate quoted for users past their first few hundred problems — the same population

serve.clear_first25.note: clear rate over positions 1-25; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.fitted_ceiling.note: 1 − the SHIPPED global lapse: the upper asymptote of the fitted response curve, which no bin of finite gap reaches

serve.gap_100_300.note: mean rating gap over positions 101-300; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gap_25_100.note: mean rating gap over positions 26-100; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gap_after300.note: mean rating gap past position 300; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gap_first25.note: mean rating gap over positions 1-25; mean of (the player's own anchor rating − the problem's shipped rating) in rating units, positive when the problem sits BELOW the player; the anchor is their 80%-clear rating fitted over their WHOLE first-time history, so a player needs at least 20 rated attempts and a mixed record to enter; first-time attempts, one row per (user, problem), by 1-based position in the user's own first-time history

serve.gapbin_clear_above2.note: clear rate where the player sits more than 2 rating units ABOVE the problem (gap >= 2); first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_clear_below2.note: clear rate where the player sits more than 2 rating units BELOW the problem (gap < -2); first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_clear_zero.note: clear rate within 0.1 of a rating unit of zero gap; in-sample, the player's anchor being fitted on these same attempts; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_inversions.note: adjacent gap bins across the whole ladder whose clear rate FALLS as the gap rises; 0 is the monotone rise the response model implies

serve.gapbin_se_above2.note: ± on serve.gapbin_clear_above2; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_se_below2.note: ± on serve.gapbin_clear_below2; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.gapbin_se_zero.note: ± on serve.gapbin_clear_zero; first-time clear rate in one bin of (player anchor rating − problem rating), bins half-open [lo, hi) in rating units; ± is the binomial standard error of that bin

serve.lapse_bound.note: largest global lapse the log admits: no attempt can clear more often than 1 − lapse, so the top gap bin's clear rate bounds it from above at 1 − that rate

serve.lapse_headroom.note: the log's lapse bound ÷ the shipped lapse — how far inside the bound the fitted value sits

serve.onboard_const_over3_pct.note: share served more than 3 ranks above true rank under a constant margin of 5 (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_const_over5_pct.note: share served more than 5 ranks above true rank under a constant margin of 5 (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_count_over3_pct.note: share served more than 3 ranks above true rank under a margin growing with the attempt count (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_dan_attempts.note: first-time attempts before an unlimited-strength solver's SHOWN rank reaches 1 dan, under the shipped serve-gap cap

serve.onboard_dan_attempts_const.note: the same under a constant margin of 5

serve.onboard_dan_attempts_count.note: the same under a margin growing with the attempt count

serve.onboard_over3_pct.note: share served more than 3 ranks above true rank under the shipped serve-gap cap (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

serve.onboard_over5_pct.note: share served more than 5 ranks above true rank under the shipped serve-gap cap (simulated 20k, first 30 first-time attempts, 2000 seeded runs on the shipped 9×9 corpus)

swing.pass_only_baseline.note: published problems whose only resolved refutation is the pass, so excluding it would leave no ownership-swing measurement at all

swing.pass_outranks_stones_pct.note: share of the published problems where a resolved pass is the swing baseline over at least one resolved stone move

window.span_max_days.note: longest span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many; bounded from above by the length of the log

window.span_median_days.note: median span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many

window.span_over_90d.note: share of those users whose window spans more than 90 days; span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many

window.span_p75_days.note: upper-quartile span in days of a FULL rank-estimator window — the 500 most recent first-time attempts — over the users who have that many

_about: Measured figures the documents quote, one key per number. Written by `python -m ablations`; raw `value` + `fmt` are the record, `text` is derived. Never edit by hand — re-run the producer.
